answer: Standing is drawn in pigment, and pigment cannot be erased once dried. Each identity must record its work with two countersigning peers outside its cluster, and a single palette may mark only one identity, so n aliases need n distinct palettes and cannot recycle one seal. At each dawn the network samples a random stroke and demands the original ivory ticket behind it; a stroke whose ticket resolves to a shared funder is voided and every mark from that palette fades. The k-th stroke costs k squared in bond, so farming pays near n cubed while pooling collapses to one identity.
